name: Arza
overview: Arza was a male figure known for his role overseeing the household at Tirzah, a significant city in the northern kingdom of Israel. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. The brief mention of Arza highlights his administrative responsibility rather than family or tribal identity.
namesAndTitles: The name Arza is a proper name that may mean 'gracious,' though this is not definitively stated. The name itself does not carry a special title or divine naming significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Arza beyond his role as the overseer of the household at Tirzah. No relatives or descendants are mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Arza's significance lies in his administrative position during a turbulent period in Israel's history, serving as the official in charge of the royal household at Tirzah. This role suggests a measure of trust and authority within the northern kingdom's governance. Although briefly mentioned, Arza's function contributes to the understanding of the political and social structure under King Baasha's reign.
